slides.text: Every spell cost a memory. That was the oldest law of magic. Apprentice wizards forgot little things—a favorite meal, an old song, the face of a childhood friend. The greatest wizard who ever lived had cast thousands of spells. By the time kingdoms began calling him a legend, he could no longer remember why he had started learning magic in the first place.

When a monstrous army marched toward the capital, the king begged the old wizard to save them one final time. The wizard quietly asked, 'Who are you?' Nobody laughed. Everyone knew another spell would erase another piece of him forever. He studied the frightened children hiding behind the soldiers and nodded. 'Whoever I once was... I think I would have helped.'

The battle lasted only minutes. Mountains split, storms bent to his will, and the invaders fled. As the dust settled, the old man looked around in wonder. 'What a beautiful world,' he whispered. 'I wish I could remember ever seeing it before.' He walked away smiling, a stranger carrying the memories of everyone else but none of his own.
